title: Integral hypersurface presentation of a separable function field
statement: A field K, an integral affine scheme Y, and a locally finite type morphism p:Y -> Spec K are given. Assume p is geometrically reduced. There exist n and Q in K[t_1,...,t_n] such that Z=Spec(K[t_1,...,t_n]/(Q)) is integral. For the coefficient-induced map q:Z -> Spec K there is a ring equivalence Frac(Gamma(Y)) -> Frac(Gamma(Z)) fixing every base section: e(iota_Y(p.appTop(a)))=iota_Z(q.appTop(a)). No geometric irreducibility hypothesis or conclusion is asserted. The notions are fields [def-pc-field-extension], affine spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum], finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], integral schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme], and polynomial rings [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring].

proof.text: Use the pullback on sections and GammaSpecIso to give B = Gamma(Y) its K-algebra structure. The affine finite-type criterion makes B finite type. Its canonical fraction ring F is essentially finite type. Identify Y with Spec B; geometric reducedness makes every field tensor E tensor_K B reduced using pullbackSpecIso and affine_isReduced_iff. Field tensor E tensor_K F is a localization, hence reduced by isReduced_tensorProduct_of_isLocalization.

Produce a finite separating transcendence basis of F/K. In characteristic zero apply the perfect-field theorem. In prime characteristic choose p-th roots of the coefficients of a finite dependence in an algebraic closure. The associated tensor has zero p-th power, so is zero by reducedness. Scalar extension preserves independence, so all roots and all coefficients vanish. Apply Mathlib exists_isTranscendenceBasis_and_isSeparable_of_linearIndepOn_pow_of_essFiniteType.

Enumerate the finite basis by Fin r. Its intermediate field E has F algebraic and separable. Finite field generation makes F finite-dimensional over E. The primitive element theorem supplies y. Put v = (y,t); its field adjoin is all F. Choose a nonzero relation Q with minimal total degree. Mathlib irreducible_of_forall_totalDegree_le makes Q irreducible. Every element of F is a ratio of polynomial evaluations in v. This adapts GenericIrreducibility.exists_hypersurface_of_perfectField, retaining all steps after its separating-basis input.

For A = K[Fin (r+1)]/(Q), irreducibility makes the defining ideal prime and A a domain. Evaluation induces an algebra hom A to F. GenericIrreducibility.dvd_of_aeval_eq_zero shows every relation belongs to (Q), proving injectivity. Lift to FractionRing A; the polynomial-ratio representation proves surjectivity. Obtain a K-algebra equivalence FractionRing A with F.

Spec A is integral. Extend the canonical ring equivalence A with Gamma(Spec A) to fraction rings, and compose it with the inverse of the K-algebra equivalence from the preceding step. For a base section, write it as GammaSpecIso.inv(c). Algebra-equivalence commutation and ringEquivOfRingEquiv_algebraMap reduce the required equality to GammaSpecIso_inv_naturality. All local helpers and the assigned theorem are proved; no new holed statement is used.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_integral_field_hypersurface_presentation
    {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine Y] [IsIntegral Y]
    (p : Y ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [LocallyOfFiniteType p]
    (hred : GeometricallyReduced p) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (Q : MvPolynomial (Fin n) K),
      let Z := Spec (.of (MvPolynomial (Fin n) K ⧸ Ideal.span {Q}))
      let q : Z ⟶ Spec (.of K) := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
        ((Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {Q})).comp MvPolynomial.C))
      IsIntegral Z ∧
        ∃ e : FractionRing Γ(Y, ⊤) ≃+* FractionRing Γ(Z, ⊤),
          ∀ a : Γ(Spec (.of K), ⊤),
            e (algebraMap Γ(Y, ⊤) (FractionRing Γ(Y, ⊤)) (p.appTop.hom a)) =
              algebraMap Γ(Z, ⊤) (FractionRing Γ(Z, ⊤)) (q.appTop.hom a)
